# Assay compiler and chromosome-haplotype model

## Forward assay model

```text
diploid chromosome-haplotype pair
    -> primer binding and compiled PCR products
    -> amplification efficiency and dropout
    -> observed ONT molecules
    -> primer, sequence, product, and artifact evidence
    -> ranked genotype classes
```

An assay profile declares primers, expected orientation, length bounds, pools and
required products. The compiler performs in-silico PCR against sequence-resolved
chromosome haplotypes and emits exact product sequences, product multiplicities,
primer mismatches, assay-coverage gaps and genotype pairs that are intrinsically
indistinguishable under the assay.

## HBA family coordinates

The HBA family-coordinate map is generated from FASTA sequences rather than kept as
a hand-written population table. HBA1, HBA2, hybrid and candidate-copy sequences
are aligned to a declared anchor; substitutions, insertions and deletions remain
explicit. The map supports copy-marker interpretation and coordinate projection.
Exact compiled product sequences remain the primary likelihood objects.

## Molecule evidence

FASTQ molecules are oriented from terminal primers and classified as complete,
one-ended, unexpected-length, primer-dimer, chimera-candidate or off-target.
Complete molecules are compared with the compiled product sequences while retaining
equivalent haplotypes, low-margin assignments and unexplained residuals.

## Genotype posterior

The state is an unordered pair of chromosome haplotypes. Variable alpha-globin copy
number is encoded inside each chromosome-haplotype sequence; human chromosome
ploidy remains two. Named pairs with the same count-aware product signature are
collapsed before assigning the default prior.

The model combines molecule compatibility, capped effective evidence for PCR
non-independence, a Dirichlet-multinomial product-composition term, relative product
efficiencies and required-product dropout. It returns one of four states:
`RESOLVED_RESEARCH_CALL`, `AMBIGUOUS_ASSAY_EQUIVALENT`,
`AMBIGUOUS_POSTERIOR`, or `NO_CALL_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`.

The production scorer is the required Cython kernel `cython_grouped_v1`; there is
no second runtime backend.
